reference: Every year in our town, people walk with lanterns on the first night of the moon festival. This year, I heard two different stories about why we do this. My neighbor, Mrs. Chen, is 78. She told me that long ago, farmers carried lanterns to their fields. They were looking for lost animals while the sun was going down. She said, "We were helping each other. The lanterns were small, but the night was dark." Her story is about kindness. My friend Leo heard a different story from his grandfather. Leo's grandfather said that people carried lanterns to remember a famous teacher who lived in the mountains. The teacher taught children who had no school. While the teacher was walking home one evening, a storm came. People walked with lights to help him find the road. Leo said, "The teacher was very important to the village."
